name: TSMC Advanced Backend Fab 7, Chiayi

summary: TSMC's advanced packaging site in the Chiayi Science Park at Taibao, Chiayi County, which the company aims to make its largest packaging fab. In March 2024 the government announced two TSMC packaging plants there, the first for CoWoS, and TSMC confirmed the plan. Work on the first plant began in May 2024 but stopped in June after suspected archaeological remains turned up, so the second plant went ahead first. Equipment installation began in the second half of 2025, and at a July 2026 ceremony officials said mass production had started in June 2026. At the same event, the groundbreaking of the park's second-phase site, officials said TSMC would build more packaging plants there (Reuters reported two, the Central News Agency three). Trade press ties the site to SoIC, WMCM and, later, CoPoS packaging.

milestones.note: The vice premier announced two TSMC packaging plants for the Chiayi Science Park, and TSMC confirmed it planned packaging capacity there.
Local authorities said on 17 June 2024 that work on the first plant had stopped after a suspected archaeological site was found; trade press later said the delay let the second plant start first.

TVBS, reporting from a January 2026 TSMC media tour, said equipment installation began at the Phase 1 plant in December; trade press says the second plant (P2) took equipment first, in the second half of 2025, because of the first plant's delay.
Trade press target for equipment move-in at the delayed first plant, with mass production there in 2027.
Reports differ on whether one or both Phase I plants were producing; Reuters said the second plant was expected to follow soon.

Groundbreaking for the second-phase site of the Chiayi Science Park, about 90 hectares, where officials said TSMC would add packaging plants; TechNews reported a second-phase packaging plant already under construction.

notes: Two counts of the second-phase plants circulate: Reuters quoted the science minister describing a third and fourth plant, while the Central News Agency reported three more facilities. Reports also differ on whether one or both first-phase plants were producing by July 2026 and on which of them took equipment first. Trade press numbers the Chiayi build-out in up to eight plants (P1 to P8), which do not match the science park's Phase I and Phase II sites; phase labels in this record follow the science park's phases except where a source names a specific plant. TSMC itself has not said which Chiayi plants are producing; the July 2026 production reports rest on statements by officials at the park ceremony.
